title: extractHTMLText
summary: Extract visible text from HTML code or htmlTree objects.

gpu_support.notes: `extractHTMLText` parses host-resident text and does not use provider kernels.

description: `extractHTMLText` extracts visible text from HTML code or from an `htmlTree` object. It supports the documented `ExtractionMethod` option values `"tree"`, `"article"`, and `"all-text"`.
behaviors: `extractHTMLText(code)` accepts string scalars, character vectors, string arrays, multi-row character arrays, and cell arrays of character vectors.
`extractHTMLText(tree)` accepts scalar RunMat `htmlTree` objects created by `htmlTree`.
String arrays, multi-row character arrays, and cell arrays return string arrays with the input shape.
Script, style, noscript, template, and head content is excluded from extracted text.
Common HTML entities and numeric character references are decoded.
`tree` and `article` currently use the same paragraph/block extraction heuristic. RunMat does not yet implement MathWorks' exact article scoring algorithm.
`all-text` extracts normalized body text outside skipped elements. Whitespace is normalized for MATLAB-friendly string output.

examples.input:
code = "

THE SONNETS

by William Shakespeare

"; str = extractHTMLText(code)

faqs.question: Are `tree` and `article` exact MATLAB article extraction modes?
faqs.answer: No. Both modes currently use RunMat's paragraph/block extraction heuristic. Exact article scoring remains part of the broader Text Analytics compatibility work.

faqs.question: Does `extractHTMLText` support arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes. Text arrays and cells produce string arrays with the same shape. Cells containing `htmlTree` objects are also supported.

faqs.question: Does `extractHTMLText` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. HTML extraction is host text processing and has no `runmat-accelerate` provider path.

example.input:
str = extractHTMLText(code)
str = extractHTMLText(tree)
str = extractHTMLText(___, 'ExtractionMethod', method)
example.output: `str` is a string scalar or string array.

points: The option name is case-insensitive and must be `ExtractionMethod`.

gpu_residency: `extractHTMLText` parses host-resident text and has no provider kernel.
